localities.name: Kolathur
localities.plot_band_note: IMPORTANT - the roofandfloor Kolathur plot page is heavily padded with listings that are NOT in North-Chennai Kolathur. I dropped seven of its ten rows (GTK Eutopia Smart City 2,793, New Star City 2,899, Om Lakshmi Nagar Annex 2,700, Aishwaryam Township 2,500, i5 CK Madhavan Nagar 1,932-3,200, RWD Elite Avenue 4,798, Premier KVT Township 5,100) because they sit 2-4x below the verified Kolathur land field - these are almost certainly outer-belt layouts (there is a second Kolathur near Tiruvallur) surfaced as 'nearby'. I also dropped Silversky Springs, quoted at 15,483/sqft: recomputing gives 1.2Cr/775 = 15,484 but 1.44Cr/1,447 = 9,952, i.e. internally inconsistent, which means the price includes BUILT villa area, not raw land. That is exactly the outlier pattern to reject. What survives is a tight, internally consistent field: two named layouts plus four search-visible vacant-plot rates, spanning 8,530-10,499 - reported as the band since n=6 is too thin to trim further.
localities.price_band_note: Apartment BUILT-UP rate. Apartment rates read 7,000-11,000/sqft with an average of 8,050/sqft (Aug 2026), up from ~7,700/sqft in Apr 2026; independent houses command 9,000-13,000/sqft. I trimmed the 11,000 top edge to 10,000 as it reflects a handful of new premium launches rather than the body of the market. Note we track 7 plot projects and ZERO apartment projects here, yet the apartment resale market is the dominant product - a coverage gap worth closing.
localities.band_audit: The existing band 6,500-8,500 is a genuine APARTMENT BUILT-UP rate, correctly labelled, but it is now stale - apartments moved +12.6% YoY and the current field is 7,000-10,000. Separately, be aware that in Kolathur LAND (8,500-10,500) trades ABOVE built-up (7,000-10,000). That inversion is normal for a dense, fully built-out inner locality where land is the scarce input, and it is the opposite of the outer-belt localities in this set where land is roughly half of built-up. Do not 'correct' it.
localities.trend_note: Apartments +12.6% YoY with the broader locality appreciating 7-9% annually on Inner Ring Road commercial growth, storm-water drainage upgrades and Madhavaram metro-hub proximity.

localities.name: Thoraipakkam

localities.name: Mangadu
localities.plot_band_note: Unusually tight and mutually confirming. All three named Mangadu layouts recompute to essentially the same rate: VLC Karikala Cholan Nagar 39.99L/800 = 4,999; Thiya Garden 39.99L/800 = 4,999; Nu Tech Samruddhi 50.4L/1,008 = 5,000. An IQR of three identical values is degenerate, so I widened to the independently reported 99acres land range of 4,550-5,600, which brackets the layouts symmetrically. TRAP CAUGHT: chennaiproperties lists a Kovur parcel at a quoted '80,000/sqft' - recomputing 1.6Cr/2,000 gives 8,000/sqft, a 10x error in the source's own per-sqft field, and it is Kovur not Mangadu. Dropped on both grounds. Only 2 plot projects tracked here versus 71 in neighbouring Kundrathur, so Mangadu is a much smaller land market at a ~50% higher rate.
localities.price_band_note: Apartment BUILT-UP rate, unchanged and re-verified: 99acres range 5,250-7,850/sqft, average 6,450/sqft. 1BHK 19.9L-49.03L, 2BHK 44.85L-72.3L. 71+ apartments listed, so a genuine resale/low-rise apartment market exists even though we track zero RERA apartment projects here - a coverage gap, not an absence of market.
localities.band_audit: The cleanest of the existing records. The band 5,250-7,850 is a genuine APARTMENT BUILT-UP rate, correctly labelled, and still current. Its note already separated the plotted-land rate (4,550-5,600/sqft) rather than conflating the two, and my three named layouts land at ~5,000/sqft, right inside that range. No correction needed - only promotion of the land figure out of the note and into a proper plot band.
localities.trend_note: Slower and steadier than neighbouring Kundrathur - flats +7.5% in 1 year (vs +27.5% at Kundrathur), +24.0% in 3 years - on Porur IT spillover and the Poonamallee metro terminus ~4 km north.

localities.name: Siruvanur
localities.plot_band_note: NO USABLE DATA - and I believe the locality itself is mis-assigned rather than merely under-covered. Nothing named 'Siruvanur' surfaces as a Chennai Metropolitan Area locality on any portal, hyperlocal site or search. Two observations, offered as leads rather than conclusions: (1) the two projects we track here (Sri Balaji Avenue Phase II, Phase III) carry RERA numbers TNRERA-2-LO-4118-2025 and TNRERA-2-LO-4161-2025 - district segment '2' - whereas the Chembarambakkam layout in the same dataset carries TNRERA-29-LO-4000-2025. Different district segment, which is at least consistent with these projects not being in the Chennai district group; I could not verify the TNRERA district code table, so this is suggestive only. (2) The closest real-world name match is SIRUGANUR, on the Trichy-Chennai NH in Tiruchirappalli district, ~300 km outside the CMA, where DTCP land trades at roughly Rs 250-942/sqft - an order of magnitude below any CMA rate. Searches also surfaced Siruvallur (a Perambur neighbourhood in North Chennai, not 'Far West'), Siruvalur (Ariyalur) and Siruvachur (Perambalur), none of which fit. RECOMMENDATION: pull the source RERA filings for those two projects and confirm the village/taluk/district before publishing any band. If they are Trichy-district layouts they should be dropped from the CMA dataset, not priced. I have deliberately returned no band rather than borrow a neighbour's rate.

localities.name: Chengalpattu town
localities.plot_band_note: Interquartile range of 31 named plotted layouts (n=31, median ~Rs 1,350/sqft), every rate recomputed by me as min_price/min_size and cross-checked against max_price/max_size. Dropped 4 outliers: Nammazhvar Organic (Rs 198/sqft, 9,582-43,556 sqft organic FARMLAND), The Country Village Farmland (Rs 299/sqft, 10,000 sqft farmland), Red Sandal (Rs 110/sqft, 9,200 sqft agricultural parcel) - all bulk agri land, not residential plots - and Lake View (Madurantakam Main Road, ~30km outside town). Also excluded a 6-acre bulk parcel at Rs 2.52 Cr that recomputes to Rs 96/sqft (raw agricultural aggregation). CAUTION: most portals conflate Chengalpattu TOWN with Chengalpattu DISTRICT - the generic 'chengalpattu' slug returns Thiruporur/Kelambakkam/Singaperumal Koil stock at 3-5x town rates. The working slug is 'chengalpet', not 'chengalpattu'. Corroborated by independent recomputed points: Chengalpattu 600sqft @ Rs 7.5L = Rs 1,250/sqft, Mamandur 1200sqft @ Rs 14.81L = Rs 1,234/sqft, Kayar 800sqft @ Rs 16L = Rs 2,000/sqft, plus search-snippet figures of Rs 1,800/sqft (Chengalpattu Township), Rs 1,750/sqft (Kanchipuram-Chengalpattu Rd), Rs 2,500/sqft (Kanchipuram High Rd nr SRK Cinemas), Rs 714/sqft (Mamandur), Rs 650/sqft (I5 Global City) - all inside or adjacent to the band.
localities.price_band_note: Apartment BUILT-UP asking rates. IQR of 9 credible points: Mahindra Nova 3,500; Mahindra Iris Court 4,050; NoBroker Dec-2025 4,300; NoBroker Jul-2026 5,727; Mahindra Lakewoods 6,144; Under-construction (Square Yards) 6,150; Mahindra World City 6,153; Square Yards Mar-2026 asking 6,588; Square Yards Jun-2026 apartment 6,600. Villa product sits higher at 8,400/sqft and is excluded - it is built villa, not comparable to flat built-up. Note land here is roughly ONE FIFTH of built-up rate, the widest land-to-built-up gap in this set.
localities.trend_note: Apartments flat at 0% YoY and under-construction stock DOWN 4.23% (Square Yards Jun-2026); heavy plotted-layout supply (104 RERA plot registrations tracked) is capping land appreciation, though Mahindra World City and the Siemens Gamesa industrial anchor support the floor. Villas alone show +27.87%.
localities.band_audit: The existing band [4500, 6600] genuinely measures APARTMENT BUILT-UP asking rates - it is correctly labelled and its note already flags the Square Yards asking-price skew. It is NOT contaminated by land. Its only defect was the absence of any plot band, which matters enormously here: 104 of 111 tracked projects are plotted layouts, and land trades at Rs 750-2,300/sqft, about a quarter of the apartment number. Anyone applying the 4,500-6,600 band to a plot deal would overprice land by roughly 4x. My band nudges the floor down to 4,200 to reflect Mahindra Iris Court/Nova entry stock and the NoBroker Dec-2025 reading.

localities.name: Velachery
localities.plot_band_note: THIN - only 2 plot projects tracked and Velachery has almost no remaining raw land, so this rests on 4 recomputed resale points plus a portal range. Recomputed: MGP Aditri II 2,400sqft @ Rs 1.98Cr = Rs 8,250/sqft; 1,800sqft CMDA @ Rs 1.85Cr = Rs 10,278/sqft; 1,200sqft (Mar-2026) @ Rs 2.2Cr = Rs 18,333/sqft. DROPPED two: a 1,200sqft @ Rs 70L listing recomputing to Rs 5,833/sqft, which is BELOW the Rs 9,294/sqft circle rate and therefore cannot be a genuine registrable Velachery transaction (stale or mislabelled), and the Rs 18,333/sqft point as a single premium/metro-frontage outlier. Floor anchored on the published circle rate (Rs 9,294/sqft, hexahome 2026); ceiling on the 99acres land range of Rs 10,350-14,050/sqft. Treat as indicative, not transactional.
localities.price_band_note: Apartment BUILT-UP. 99acres flat range Rs 7,300-11,600/sqft with average ~Rs 9,400; reported average TRANSACTION rate Rs 10,164/sqft; another source cites Rs 9,500 average. Luxury projects quoted above Rs 15,000/sqft are excluded as a separate premium tier, not mid-market comparables.
localities.trend_note: Mature, fully built-out market with negligible new land supply; asking rates flat year-on-year and a transacted average (Rs 10,164) sitting close to the asking midpoint, which signals a liquid but not appreciating market.
localities.band_audit: The existing band [7850, 13250] measures APARTMENT BUILT-UP and is correctly labelled - the note's ~Rs 9,500 average matches the 99acres and transaction figures. However its Rs 13,250 ceiling is luxury-skewed: the mainstream 99acres flat range tops out at Rs 11,600, and 13,250 sits inside the LAND band (9,300-13,500) rather than the mid-market flat band. Anyone reading 13,250 as a normal Velachery flat rate would overpay. I have tightened the apartment band to 8,200-11,600 and split the land rate out separately.

localities.name: Adambakkam
localities.plot_band_note: Land rate per sqft. Portal land range Rs 11,400-15,000/sqft (99acres), corroborated by the one clean recomputed comparable I could verify: 900 sqft at Rs 1.08 Cr near Puzhuthivakkam MRTS = Rs 12,000/sqft exactly. Only 4 plot projects tracked and genuine vacant land is scarce here, so comparables are few. I DISCARDED a widely-syndicated 3,132 sqft @ Rs 1.85 Cr listing (recomputes to Rs 5,907/sqft) as inconsistent with every other Adambakkam land observation and likely a mis-scraped record. NOTE the land band sits ABOVE the apartment band here - normal for a built-out inner suburb where a redevelopable plot carries FSI value.
localities.price_band_note: Apartment BUILT-UP. 99acres flat range Rs 8,550-10,900/sqft, average ~Rs 9,000; weighted average cited at Rs 10,000/sqft.
localities.trend_note: Land rates up 29.2% year-on-year against flats up only 2.9% (99acres) - a classic redevelopment-driven land squeeze, with Metro Phase 2 alignment through the Adambakkam/Puzhuthivakkam corridor pulling plot values ahead of built stock.
localities.band_audit: The existing band [8500, 12200] is labelled apartment and its floor (8,500) is a sound apartment built-up figure matching the 99acres 8,550 low. But the band is a MIX, not a clean apartment band: its Rs 12,200 ceiling exceeds the mainstream flat range (which tops at 10,900) and sits squarely inside the LAND band (11,400-15,000). The note's own reference to 'NoBroker premium pockets up to Rs 19,400' is almost certainly a land or ultra-premium figure, not mid-market flat built-up. So the upper half of the existing band is land/premium contamination and should not be used to price a flat.

localities.name: Anumanthaputheri
localities.plot_band_note: NO USABLE MARKET BAND FOUND - deliberately returning found:false rather than a fabricated figure. What I did establish: Anumanthaputheri is a revenue village in CHENGALPATTU taluk (Chengalpattu district), not the Kanchipuram corridor as currently tagged in the dataset - worth correcting. The tnlandlord.in village page for it exists but renders navigation only, with no prices. The ONLY price-like figure anywhere is a third-party guideline-value mirror quoting Rs 1,650/sqft for 'Anumanthaputheri Nadu Street' dated 2024, and per the brief a GV from a stale third-party mirror is weak corroboration only, never a market rate. Notably it CONTRADICTS the 2-3x-GV heuristic here: 2x of 1,650 would imply ~Rs 3,300/sqft, far above the Rs 750-2,300 band I measured across 31 real Chengalpattu-town layouts, so the mirror is likely stale or mis-keyed. No portal slug exists (roofandfloor, chennaiproperties, sulekha, nestoria all return nothing for this village). The three tracked projects are all registry-only plotted layouts (NS Nagar Virivu I/II/III by K. Nithiyanandam) with no pricing. NEAREST DEFENSIBLE PROXY, to be used only as context and NOT written in as this locality's band: the Chengalpattu-town layout belt at Rs 750-2,300/sqft.
localities.price_band_note: No apartment market - zero apartment projects tracked and none found in research. Correctly null; the land proxy must NOT be copied across.

localities.name: Vengambakkam
localities.plot_band_note: IQR of 5 recomputed comparables (median Rs 4,800/sqft). Rates recomputed by me: Dollars Colony Phase 2 Rs 40.57L/712 = Rs 5,698; Grand Avenue Rs 50L/1,200 = Rs 4,167 rising to Rs 1.24Cr/2,400 = Rs 5,167 (this one is NOT a flat marketing rate, so I carried both ends); individual 3,750sqft plot Rs 1.8Cr = Rs 4,800; Maxworth Zion 150 Rs 44.25L/924 = Rs 4,789. NOTE the dataset tags this GST Road, but Vengambakkam actually sits on the Vandalur-Kelambakkam road near Mappedu/Rathinamangalam - worth checking the corridor label.
localities.price_band_note: Apartment BUILT-UP, THIN - only 1 apartment project tracked. Anchored on the 99acres weighted average of Rs 5,550/sqft for Vengambakkam, plus the one curated project: Casagrand Estia, which I recomputed from its own price/size ranges as Rs 52L/1,076 = Rs 4,833 to Rs 72L/1,589 = Rs 4,531 per sqft. Land and built-up sit unusually close here, which is genuine for an inner-periphery node with expensive land and modest built product, not contamination.
localities.trend_note: Apartment prices up 11.0% in the last year (99acres) on Vandalur-Kelambakkam road widening and OMR/GST cross-connectivity; plotted supply is still absorbing at Rs 4,800-5,700.

localities.name: Orikkai

That inversion is unusual and important: the general rule that Chennai land trades at a third of built-up does not hold here, because Medavakkam's remaining plotted supply is scarce, junction-adjacent and metro-facing while its apartment stock is mid-market builder product. Anyone applying a land-vs-flat ratio heuristic to this locality will get it badly wrong.

localities.trend_note: 99acres puts the Padur average at Rs 7,658/sqft in July 2026 against an existing record band topping out at 6,500 — corridor-wide OMR absorption plus branded entries (Godrej, TVS Emerald, Urbanrise) have repriced the micro-market upward; adjacent Kelambakkam is quoted at +15.8% YoY.
localities.band_audit: The existing 4,200-6,500 band IS an apartment built-up band and is correctly typed — no land contamination. But its own note admits it was 'estimated between Siruseri and Kelambakkam levels', i.e. corridor-inferred rather than locality-sourced, and it is now materially stale on the low side: eight named Padur projects and three independent portals all put the 2026 apartment market at 5,900-8,300/sqft. The band's ceiling (6,500) is now roughly the market's floor-to-median.

localities.name: Anakaputhur
localities.plot_band_note: LAND rate per sqft. THIN — only 2 genuinely Anakaputhur-labelled comparables exist across the working sources, so this is an anchored band rather than a true IQR. Floor = Sri Radha Nagar (Annai Builders, Bakthavachalam Road), which I recomputed as 19.8L/600 = 3,300 AND 39.6L/1200 = 3,300, confirmed identically on both roofandfloor and chennaiproperties, and matched by a separate search listing at 3,300/sqft near Sri Sakthi Sai Baba Karunalayam. Ceiling = 99acres' published Anakaputhur land range of Rs 3,500-5,100/sqft (2025-26). The one other Anakaputhur parcel I found — 2,328 sqft near the Anakaputhur Register Office at Rs 1.28 Cr — recomputes to 5,498/sqft; I treated it as main-road/register-office frontage sitting just above the residential band rather than as typical layout product. NOTE the fetch tool reported that parcel's rate as '55,000/sqft' — a factor-of-ten error of exactly the kind flagged; the real figure is 5,498. IMPORTANT: roofandfloor's Anakaputhur page and realnest's Anakaputhur page are almost entirely Kundrathur / Pallavaram / Tharapakkam fill (realnest states outright 'No matching properties in Anakaputhur'); I excluded all of it, including KG Kingdom Of Prosperity (2,499), Urban Tree Crystal Crowns (2,999), NuTech Inscape (4,500), VGN Highland (4,798) and Rajparis Aeroville (7,499).

plot_comparables.layout: Individual parcel near Anakaputhur Register Office (main-road frontage)

localities.price_band_note: APARTMENT built-up rate, but a THIN market — zero organised apartment projects are tracked here and supply is small builder-floor stock, not gated developments. No named apartment project with a recomputable price+size could be found on any working source. Band is anchored on two portal averages only: the ~Rs 5,550/sqft flat average already in the record, and 99acres' 2026 Anakaputhur figure of Rs 6,000/sqft. Treat as indicative; buyers should price street by street given the Adyar-riverbank flood exposure.
localities.trend_note: 99acres 2026 shows Anakaputhur at +30.4% YoY (vs neighbouring Pammal +11.6%) — treat the magnitude with caution as it is almost certainly amplified by listing mix rather than genuine repricing, but the direction is a clear change from the 'stable' currently recorded.
localities.band_audit: The existing 4,150-5,950 band is an APARTMENT/flat built-up band — it is built around the ~Rs 5,550/sqft flat average, and the land rate (3,500-5,100) appears only in the note and was NOT folded into the band. So it is not contaminated. The real problem is fitness for purpose: Anakaputhur tracks 4 plot projects and 0 apartment projects, so the locality is being represented by a built-up rate for a product type that barely exists there. The land figure sitting unused in its own note is the number that should have been the band.

localities.name: Peerkankaranai
localities.plot_band_note: LAND rate per sqft — ESTIMATED, weakest band in this batch. Peerkankaranai has no roofandfloor or chennaiproperties slug and only 1 usable locality-labelled data point. Derivation, stated in full so it can be checked: (a) a CMDA-approved 1,200 sqft plot listed on Sulekha under Peerkankaranai/Tambaram at Rs 3,599/sqft (approx Rs 43.19L) — this is Sulekha's own quoted per-sqft field, which I could NOT independently recompute because the listing gives no separate total, so it inherits the exact defect flagged in the brief and I weight it accordingly; (b) adjoining Tambaram West layouts quoted at Rs 2,999/sqft over a Rs 21.56L-53.90L range, which recomputes self-consistently to 719-1,797 sqft and gives a credible floor for the belt; (c) an upper bound constraint — the locality's blended registry average is Rs 4,652/sqft across 59 transactions, and since that average includes built product (flats and houses) the raw land rate must sit below it. Hence 3,000-4,000. Do not treat this as a sourced market band; it is a reasoned interval between two anchors.

plot_comparables.layout: CMDA-approved plot, Peerkankaranai (Sulekha listing, no project name)

localities.price_band_note: APARTMENT built-up rate. No named Peerkankaranai apartment project with a recomputable price+size is published on any working source, so this carries over the two figures already in the record and re-verified this pass: the Rs 4,652/sqft registry average over 59 transactions (which is blended across property types and therefore a soft floor for flats) and the ~Rs 5,500/sqft asking rate for new 2BHKs at roughly Rs 37-43 lakh. Only 1 apartment project is tracked here; supply is small-builder.
localities.trend_note: No locality-level trend series is published for Peerkankaranai by any source I could reach — 99acres carries the transaction average but no 1yr/3yr/5yr change. Recording 'stable' as an absence of evidence, not evidence of flatness.
localities.band_audit: The existing 4,500-5,500 band is MIXED, not a clean apartment band. Its floor (~4,652) is a registry average across ALL property types transacting in the locality — land, flats and independent houses together — while its ceiling (5,500) is a flat asking rate for new 2BHKs. So the two endpoints are not measuring the same thing: one is blended-transacted, the other is apartment-asking. It is not a land band and should not be used as one, but it is also not a defensible pure apartment band.

localities.name: Avadi
localities.plot_band_note: LAND rate per sqft. Strongest plot dataset in this batch: IQR of 21 named Avadi layouts on roofandfloor.com, per-sqft recomputed by me from total price / plot size at BOTH ends of every listing. Median 4,299; full spread 2,700 (Sri Sai City) to 6,101 (Dura Sakthi Garden). No outliers dropped — all 21 are genuine DTCP/CMDA layout product in the same size class, and the IQR already trims the tails. Krish Classic City's quoted 5,100 recomputes to ~5,245 at both ends; I used the computed figure.
localities.price_band_note: APARTMENT built-up rate. IQR of 10 named Avadi listings on chennaiproperties.com (8 projects + 2 resale), per-sqft recomputed by me from total price / size. Median 6,168; full spread 3,800 (Hazel, Hazel Realty) to 8,037 (MCB Marvel — small 441-535 sqft 1BHK units carrying the usual small-unit premium). Corroborated by 99acres 2026 Avadi flat average of Rs 5,900/sqft. spiritofchennai's 2026 guide quotes 3,800-5,500 and now looks low. Two portal per-sqft fields were badly wrong and I overrode both: Newry Altura quoted 6,500 but computes to ~7,455 across four configurations, and DRA Urbania quoted 4,999 but computes to ~6,135. I did NOT use 99acres' claimed 'average transaction rate of Rs 10,770/sqft' for Avadi — a transacted rate 83% ABOVE the asking average is not credible and is a portal artefact.
localities.trend_note: 99acres 2026 shows +8.3% over 1yr, +24.2% over 3yr, +47.5% over 5yr — a real but much calmer figure than the +21.6% YoY currently recorded, which supports the existing caution that the older number was new-launch-mix amplified.
localities.band_audit: The existing 4,000-6,500 band IS an apartment built-up band, correctly typed, and its note correctly warns that plots are cheaper — no land contamination. It is now stale on the low side: its stated '~Rs 4,500/sqft average' has been overtaken by 99acres' 2026 average of Rs 5,900 and by my 10-listing IQR of 5,500-6,650. The 'plots cheaper' claim is CONFIRMED and now quantified — Avadi land runs 3,600-5,000/sqft, i.e. roughly 60-75% of built-up.

localities.name: Keelkattalai
localities.plot_band_note: LAND rate per sqft — SINGLE-SOURCE, use with care. 99acres (2026) publishes Keelkattalai land at Rs 10,650-12,000/sqft. I could not corroborate it with a named layout: roofandfloor's Keelkattalai plot page returns ZERO Keelkattalai listings, filling instead with Pallavaram (Urban Tree Diamond Kingdom, 5,299), Pallikaranai (Iyra Anuhya 5,349; MGPs Tuscany 4,650) and Chromepet (OmShakthy Industrial Park, 4,500) — all recomputed by me, all excluded as wrong locality. That gap is itself the finding: Keelkattalai is a built-out established suburb with no organised plotted-layout supply left, so its land trades as scarce individual infill parcels at ~1.2-1.4x the local built-up rate, while new layout product in the surrounding belt sells at less than half that. Only 1 plot project is tracked here, so effort was allocated accordingly.
localities.price_band_note: APARTMENT built-up rate. IQR of 8 named Keelkattalai listings on chennaiproperties.com, per-sqft recomputed by me from total price / size. Median 8,000; full spread 6,800 (Mithun Sunshine) to 9,465 (Perfect Paramesh). Every listing is street-labelled inside Keelkattalai, so no locality bleed. Corroborated by 99acres' Keelkattalai flat average of Rs 8,750/sqft, which sits inside this band. 99acres' wider quoted range of 7,700-11,100 has a higher ceiling than my sample reaches; the 11,100 reflects premium and large-format listings not present among these eight.
localities.trend_note: 99acres 2026 confirms +10.1% over 1yr, +23.2% over 3yr, +66.7% over 5yr — the strongest sustained 5-year run of the eight localities here, driven by the 200ft Medavakkam-Pallavaram radial road and near-exhausted land supply.
localities.band_audit: The existing 7,700-11,100 band IS an apartment built-up band and is cleanly typed — its endpoints are exactly 99acres' published flat range for the locality, and the stated ~Rs 8,750/sqft average is the flat average. No land contamination. The one thing the record does not say, and must: Keelkattalai LAND is a completely separate and HIGHER number (10,650-12,000/sqft), so this apartment band overlaps the land band numerically and could easily be misread as covering plots. It does not.

localities.name: Nedungundram
localities.plot_band_note: LAND rate per sqft. Two independent anchors, both recomputable: (a) three Sulekha listings under Nedunkundram at 800 sqft/Rs 36L, 1,000 sqft/Rs 45L and 1,200 sqft/Rs 54L — each recomputes to exactly 4,500/sqft, self-consistent but probably one seller or one layout, so I count it as a single observation; (b) Merloam Estates Easton Enclave at Nedungundram-Perungalathur, CMDA + RERA approved, 3 acres / 76 plots / 445-1,577 sqft, base rate Rs 5,500/sqft. The gap between them is the approval-and-brand premium. IMPORTANT TRAP AVOIDED: a search snippet reported 'rates as low as Rs 150/sqft for corner plots in Nedungundram' — that is not a rate, it is Merloam's corner-plot PREMIUM (their published add-ons are North Rs 75, East Rs 75, corner Rs 150, 40ft road Rs 200 per sqft on top of the 5,500 base). Reading it as a land rate would understate the market by ~97%. Also excluded: a Gandhi Road parcel at Rs 63.72L with no stated area, which cannot be recomputed. Note the effective all-in cost is above the band — Merloam adds guideline value at Rs 4,000 and registration at 9%.

plot_comparables.layout: Sulekha listings, Nedunkundram (no project name; 800/1000/1200 sqft at Rs 36L/45L/54L)

localities.price_band_note: NO APARTMENT MARKET. Nedungundram is a plotted-layout village pocket between New Perungalathur and Vandalur; both tracked projects are plotted layouts and no organised apartment supply exists or is listed there on any source. Nearest apartment supply is New Perungalathur / Vandalur. Apartment band deliberately left null rather than copying the land rate across.
localities.trend_note: No trend series is published for Nedungundram by any source. The 4,500 vs 5,500 spread between unbranded and RERA-approved product is suggestive of firming but is a product-quality difference, not a time series, so no direction is claimed.

localities.name: Gummidipoondi
localities.plot_band_note: LAND rate per sqft. Anchors: (a) Peddikuppam, Gummidipoondi — 600 sqft at Rs 9,60,000, which I recomputed as 1,600/sqft (Sulekha DTCP listing, Moon Realtors, Ramky Fab City referenced); (b) branded DTCP + RERA approved villa plots, 600-2,000 sqft, asking Rs 2,275/sqft; (c) a reported Rs 1,300/sqft tier for ordinary approved layouts. DROPPED as a different product class, not residential plot: the acre-scale parcels on the same Sulekha page — 45 acres/Rs 90 Cr, 21 acres/Rs 36.75 Cr, 15 acres/Rs 28.50 Cr — which I recomputed to Rs 459, 402 and 436 per sqft respectively; these are agricultural/industrial bulk land and would collapse the band by ~70% if left in. Also dropped: everything on that page labelled Minjur, Ponneri, Vengal or Periyapalayam (wrong locality), and a reported Rs 5,000/sqft figure which is town-centre/main-road frontage rather than layout product. The ~Rs 900/sqft floor in the existing record is the unapproved/far-patta tail, below the working approved-layout market. Beware the marketed-supply illusion here: 7,100+ plot listings on OLX alone against genuine absorption that is a small fraction of that.

plot_comparables.layout: Peddikuppam, Gummidipoondi (Ramky Fab City area; DTCP)
DTCP + RERA approved villa plots, Gummidipoondi (no project name in listing)

localities.price_band_note: NO APARTMENT MARKET — confirmed again this pass. No apartment supply is listed for Gummidipoondi on any working source, and the one tracked project is a plotted layout. spiritofchennai's 2026 Chennai apartment guide does not carry Gummidipoondi at all. Band left null rather than copying the land rate across.
localities.trend_note: No locality trend series is published for Gummidipoondi by any source reachable this pass — 99acres does not carry the locality and Sulekha/OLX publish listings without a price index. The existing 'rising' call on SIPCOT employment demand could not be re-verified, so no direction is claimed rather than echoing it.
localities.band_audit: The existing 900-2,275 band is already a LAND band, correctly typed, correctly labelled as plotted-land rates, and correctly states there is no apartment market — the cleanest of the pre-existing bands in this batch. The only refinement: its Rs 900 floor is the unapproved/far-patta tail rather than the working market floor. Approved DTCP layout product starts nearer Rs 1,300-1,600/sqft (verified: 600 sqft at Rs 9.6L in Peddikuppam = 1,600), so the band's bottom third describes stock most buyers should not be underwriting.

localities.name: Poonamallee
localities.plot_band_note: Interquartile range of 25 named RERA/DTCP layouts on roofandfloor + chennaiproperties, per-sqft RECOMPUTED by me as min_price/min_size and cross-checked against max_price/max_size (roofandfloor's flat marketing rate reconciled on all 25). Median 4,200. Outliers left outside the IQR: Susee Alight 1,398 (far-fringe, almost certainly toward Thirumazhisai/Mappedu rather than Poonamallee proper) and Sameera Elite Gardens 7,999 (premium gated product). CORROBORATION: 99acres publishes avg land asking 4,500/sqft and individual listings 3,199-7,000; a 1,200 sqft plot is listed at Rs 54L (=4,500/sqft). TRANSACTED reality is materially lower - the 99acres average REGISTRY rate is 2,965/sqft across 839 recent transactions, sitting exactly at my Q1. Read 3,000 as roughly the transacted level and 5,500 as top-end gated asking.

plot_comparables.developer: Raj Housing and Estates Pvt Ltd
Fomra Housing and Infrastructure Pvt Ltd
S and P Foundation Private Limited

localities.price_band_note: APARTMENT built-up rate. 99acres 2026: flats 5,150-7,450/sqft, average 6,100/sqft, average TRANSACTION rate 6,924/sqft. Flat rates +8.9% in 1yr, +17.3% 3yr, +45.2% 5yr. Note the unusual signature here: the transacted flat rate (6,924) sits ABOVE the asking average (6,100), which is the opposite of the normal asking-premium and points to genuine end-user absorption rather than speculative listing inflation.
localities.trend_note: Strongest of the eight. Land +12.5% in 1yr (+38.5% 3yr, +69.8% 5yr) and flats +8.9% in 1yr, driven by Metro Phase 2 Corridor 4 (Lighthouse-Poonamallee, 26.1km) whose western stretch is targeted to open in 2026; reporting says land within 1km of planned stations moved 20-30% in the last 18 months. CAUTION on yield: 99acres publishes an 'average rental yield in Poonamallee 6%' figure which I am NOT propagating - it fails a rent check (6% on a ~1,100 sqft flat at 6,100/sqft implies ~Rs 33,500/month, far above actual Poonamallee 2BHK rents). The 3.5% I report is a segment-typical ESTIMATE, not a sourced figure.
localities.band_audit: Existing band [5150, 7450] with note 'Apartments; average ~Rs 6,100/sqft (99acres); plots cheaper' is CORRECT and CURRENT - it genuinely measures apartment BUILT-UP rate, is correctly labelled as such, and 99acres still publishes exactly 5,150-7,450 / avg 6,100 in 2026. Its parenthetical 'plots cheaper' is also correct and now quantified: land IQR 3,000-5,500 vs flats 5,150-7,450, i.e. land runs roughly 55-75% of built-up here. No correction needed; the locality simply had no plot band, which is the gap I have now filled - and with 27 plot projects vs 2 apartment projects tracked, the plot band is the one that actually matters for this locality.

localities.name: Nungambakkam
localities.plot_band_note: LAND rate per sqft. 99acres 2026: 22,800-32,150/sqft, average 28,550/sqft; residential plot tickets Rs 6.86Cr-18.5Cr. This is a PORTAL-PUBLISHED range, not an IQR I built from named layouts - and deliberately so: Nungambakkam has no plotted layouts. Land here transacts as individual CBD bungalow plots (only 12-13 land listings exist city-portal-wide), so there are no 'layout + developer' comparables to gather, and I am not going to manufacture any. Corroboration: general reporting places the Poes Garden / Boat Club / Nungambakkam prime band at Rs 20,000-40,000+/sqft, consistent with this range. Land rates +1.4% in the last 1yr - essentially flat.
localities.price_band_note: APARTMENT built-up rate. 99acres 2026: flats 19,100-28,350/sqft, average 22,300/sqft. Independent corroboration (livehomes 2026): mid-range 20,000-24,000/sqft, high-end/luxury 25,000-35,000+/sqft; a third source gives avg 20,500. Ticket sizes: 2BHK Rs 80L-3.5Cr, 3BHK Rs 2.5-5.5Cr, 4BHK Rs 5.5-11Cr. Flats +13.5% in 1yr, +48.7% 3yr, +124.1% 5yr.
localities.trend_note: Split market, and the split matters: APARTMENTS +13.5% in 1yr (a genuinely strong move for an ultra-prime CBD pocket) while LAND is essentially static at +1.4% in 1yr. The appreciation is in built product and redevelopment, not in raw land - so the existing record's 'stable' trend is right about land and wrong about flats. Yield 2.8% is an ESTIMATE, not sourced: central Chennai yields compress because purchase prices have outrun rents, and no locality-specific yield figure was published.
localities.band_audit: Existing band [14000, 20000] with note 'Apartments; among Chennai's costliest along with Adyar and T. Nagar' IS a genuine apartment BUILT-UP band and IS correctly labelled - no land/built-up contamination. But it is materially STALE. 99acres 2026 shows 19,100-28,350 (avg 22,300): the old band's CEILING of 20,000 is now roughly the market FLOOR. With flats +13.5% in the last year alone, the old band understates the current market by roughly 30-40% and would badly mis-price any Boardroom-lens ticket built on it. Recommend replacing with 19,100-28,350. Separately, the record had no land band at all, and Nungambakkam land at 22,800-32,150 runs ABOVE built-up - so a naive reuse of the apartment number as a land rate would understate land by ~25%.

localities.name: Egattur
localities.plot_band_note: Interquartile range of 8 named layouts on chennaiproperties, per-sqft RECOMPUTED by me from min_price/min_size and verified against max_price/max_size. Median 5,375. DROPPED: (1) Cosmo Grand at 12,400/sqft - roughly double the field, premium villa-plot product rather than raw layout land; (2) an individual owner listing (1,800 sqft, Rs 2.15Cr = 11,944/sqft) which is in NAVALUR, not Egattur, and is not a layout at all. CORROBORATION: 99acres gives an average TRANSACTION rate for Egattur land of 6,250/sqft, sitting at the top of my asking IQR, and neighbouring Navalur land at 5,000-6,500/sqft. Egattur land +5.7% in 1yr, +35.8% in 5yr. Caveat: several of these 'Egattur' layouts sit in the wider Egattur-Navalur-Padur belt rather than Egattur village proper.

plot_comparables.developer: True Value Homes India Pvt Ltd

localities.price_band_note: APARTMENT built-up rate. 99acres 2026: flats 9,050-14,100/sqft, average 12,700/sqft. House of Hiranandani Upscale (the dominant project: 120 acres, 15 towers, 2,028 units, 2/3/4BHK from 683-1,595 sqft) is quoted at 13,000/sqft, with 2BHK from Rs 79.05L, 3BHK from Rs 1.05Cr, 4BHK from Rs 1.77Cr. WARNING - conflicting figure to reject: squareyards publishes an 'average price 7,400/sqft' for Hiranandani Egattur OMR (claiming a move from 5,750 during Q4'2025). That is a single-project resale-index artifact and it contradicts both 99acres and the developer's own quoted rate by ~45%. Do not use it.
localities.trend_note: Flats +19.8% in 1yr, +67.1% 3yr, +85.4% 5yr - the steepest apartment move of the eight; land +5.7% in 1yr. Driven by the Sholinganallur-SIPCOT Siruseri job corridor and the Metro Phase 2 terminal stretch to SIPCOT. Note 99acres also reports a much softer +1.9% Y-o-Y on its apartment average, so the 19.8% and 1.9% figures coexist on the same source page - the pocket is rising but the exact rate is unstable. Rental yield 3% is directly sourced (99acres).
localities.band_audit: Existing band [8500, 13000] with note 'Avg ~Rs 10,800/sqft - premium end of lower OMR (Hiranandani, Casagrand cluster)' IS a genuine apartment BUILT-UP band, correctly labelled, with no land contamination - and the 10,800 average it cites is still live on 99acres' overview page. But the rate-trends page has moved ahead to 9,050-14,100 (avg 12,700), so the band is mildly STALE at both ends, consistent with flats +19.8% over the year. Recommend 9,050-14,100. The record had no land band; at 4,700-6,500 Egattur land is roughly HALF the built-up rate, so the two must not be interchanged.

localities.name: Kizhavedu
localities.corridor: GST Road / Chengalpattu (see note - taluk correction)
localities.plot_band_note: NO USABLE LOCALITY-SPECIFIC DATA - returning found:false rather than a fabricated band. What I did establish: Kizhavedu is a village in THIRUKALUKUNDRAM taluk, Chengalpattu district (not on the GST Road spine itself - it sits east of Chengalpattu toward Mahabalipuram, so the dataset's 'GST Road' corridor label is loose). The only trace of it in any registry is TNRERA regularisation layout TN/01/Regularisation-Layout/3828/2022 (plots 31-56, 26 plots, S.Nos 81/1, 81/2 & 85/3, promoter Thiru. J. Baskaran of Chengalpet), registered May 2022. No portal carries Kizhavedu-tagged listings; roofandfloor and chennaiproperties have no slug for it. FOR CONTEXT ONLY, NOT A KIZHAVEDU BAND - the surrounding Thirukalukundram belt, per-sqft recomputed by me: raw/unapproved parcels ~556-600/sqft (3,600 sqft @ Rs 20L = 556; 845 sqft @ Rs 5.07L = 600; 670 sqft @ Rs 4.02L = 600; 800 sqft @ Rs 4.80L = 600), DTCP-approved gated product ~1,800-2,250/sqft (646 sqft @ Rs 12.26L = 1,898; 1,800 sqft @ Rs 40.5L = 2,250; one layout quoted flat at 1,800). Thirukalukundram guideline value ~800/sqft. IMPORTANT TRAP HIT HERE: a search summary of these very sulekha listings reported them as 'approximately Rs 6,000-8,000+ per sqft' - that is the known sulekha bad per-sqft field, wrong by a factor of ten. Every figure above is my own recomputation of total_price/area.
localities.price_band_note: No apartment market. Kizhavedu is a rural Chengalpattu-district revenue village; the 3 projects tracked here are all plotted layouts and 0 are apartments. Band correctly null - NOT copied from any land rate.
localities.trend_note: No locality-specific trend data found. Do not infer one from the Chengalpattu-town or GST Road corridor - Kizhavedu is off both.

localities.name: Anna Nagar
localities.plot_band_note: LAND rate per sqft. 99acres 2026: 24,250-34,900/sqft, average 27,800/sqft. Sub-market split is large and worth carrying: Anna Nagar WEST 19,250-30,850 (avg 26,400), Anna Nagar EAST 32,100-37,450 (avg 35,300) - East carries a ~34% premium over West, so a single Anna Nagar land number is coarse. Portal-published range rather than a layout IQR, for the same reason as Nungambakkam: Anna Nagar is a planned bungalow-plot neighbourhood with no plotted layouts on sale, only individual resale grounds. WEAK CORROBORATION ONLY: the published circle/guideline rate is 16,264/sqft; at the 1.2-1.5x guideline multiple that central Chennai typically trades at, that implies ~19,500-24,400/sqft, which brackets the West average and the bottom of the overall band. Treat the guideline figure as directional only. Land +12.1% 1yr, +31.8% 3yr, +51.5% 5yr.
localities.price_band_note: APARTMENT built-up rate. 99acres 2026: flats 12,700-19,500/sqft, average 15,250/sqft, +6.3% in 1yr. Second independent source (hexahome) gives avg 14,050/sqft at +4.1% YoY - close enough to treat the ~14,000-15,250 average as solid. Ticket sizes: 2BHK Rs 81.5L-1.8Cr, 3BHK Rs 2.15-3.3Cr.
localities.trend_note: Land is running well ahead of built product: +12.1% vs +6.3% in the last year. That is the signature of a supply-constrained redevelopment market - buyers are paying up for grounds to redevelop, and Anna Nagar has effectively no new land. Green Line metro, schools/hospitals/retail and a deep self-employed buyer base sustain it. Yield 3.0% is an ESTIMATE: general commentary calls 4-6% 'good' for Chennai and lists Anna Nagar among top rental-return localities, but no Anna Nagar-specific measured yield was published, and prices here have outrun rents.

localities.band_audit: MISLABELLED — this is the important audit finding in this batch. The existing band [8000, 14000] is a MIX of two different rates, and its note is factually inverted. The note reads 'Avg flat rate ~Rs 12,250/sqft (99acres range Rs 7,100-12,500)'. But 99acres reports Rs 12,250/sqft as the average LAND rate in Palavakkam, not the average flat rate — the average flat transaction is Rs 8,750/sqft. So the prior researcher took a LAND number and recorded it as the apartment average, then stretched the band up to 14,000 on the strength of it plus the beach-side villa-plot reference. Net effect: the lower bound (8,000) roughly tracks the real apartment market, while the upper bound (14,000) is a land rate wearing an apartment label. The two should be split as they now are: land Rs 10,400-13,000/sqft, built-up Rs 7,100-12,500/sqft with transacted average Rs 8,750/sqft.

localities.band_audit: The existing band [3400, 5000] IS a genuine apartment built-up band, correctly labelled — the note says 'Apartment rates; 99acres average ~Rs 3,800/sqft', and that is indeed an apartment figure, not land. So no land/built-up confusion here. Two real problems though. First, it is stale and low: it was anchored to the lagging Rs 3,800 average, whereas current asking is Rs 4,850-5,950/sqft after 10.3% YoY. Second, and more subtly, the old apartment band [3400, 5000] and the newly measured LAND band [3000, 4500] overlap almost completely — which is anomalous for Chennai, where land normally runs about a third of built-up. That coincidence is a genuine market feature here, not an error: Kattankulathur plotted land is unusually expensive relative to its flats because SRM-driven plot demand has bid land up while apartment stock stays budget-grade. Worth flagging so a future reader does not 'fix' the overlap by assuming contamination.

It is not — it sits off Medavakkam Main Road / Medavakkam-Sholinganallur Road, ~7km east of GST, and prices with Medavakkam-Sithalapakkam, not with the GST belt (Medavakkam land 5,500-7,500, Sithalapakkam layouts 4,899-5,900). Vengaivasal actually trades ABOVE both.
localities.price_band_note: IQR of 9 recomputed project comparables = 5,206-7,749, median 6,700 — brackets 99acres' locality flat range of Rs 5,700-8,050 (avg 6,450) almost exactly. Recomputed: Venishaa Enclave 4,500; ARRAs Nandhavanam 4,742; Tulive Pavilion 5,670; Kamaraj (Mithun Homes) 5,850; Ayyan Devesh (Sri Ayyan Homes, a RERA project we track) 6,700; SRM 3BHK 7,240; TVS Emerald Udyana Ph3 7,287-7,748. HIGH OUTLIERS NOTED, NOT DROPPED: Navins Starwood Towers 2 at 7,998/sqft and Starwood 3 / Maple Sky at 9,339-9,477/sqft — a large gated township on Vengaivasal Main Road that prices off Perumbakkam-Sholinganallur, not off the village. Excluding it the band tightens to roughly 4,700-7,300.
localities.trend_note: Land is the driver — adjacent Medavakkam land is +20.4% in 1yr and +80.6% in 3yr, and Vengaivasal plots now clear above Medavakkam's own 5,500-7,500 band; flats are the laggard (99acres shows apartments -0.8% over 1yr, +18.3% over 3yr).

localities.name: Kolivakkam
localities.plot_band_note: NO USABLE DATA — deliberately returning no band rather than a fabricated one. Squareyards' Kolivakkam-Kanchipuram page returns 'No results matching your search' and falls back to other villages; chennaiproperties has no Kolivakkam listings at all; roofandfloor has no Kolivakkam slug; 99acres exposes only price-filter landing pages ('Kolivakkam, Kanchipuram from 10 lakhs to 15 lakhs', 'from 10 to 20 lakhs') with no readable listings behind them, and 99acres listing pages are 403-blocked. Zero Kolivakkam-specific price/area pairs exist that I could recompute. NEAREST RECOMPUTED COMPARABLES, for context only and NOT a basis for a band: Walajabad 1,567 sqft at Rs 23.48L = Rs 1,498/sqft, and Sirukaveripakkam 3,168 sqft at Rs 95.04L = Rs 3,000/sqft (both via squareyards' fallback list). Those two adjacent villages differ by 2x, which is exactly why interpolating a Kolivakkam number would be guesswork. Kanchipuram-belt plotted layouts elsewhere quote Rs 2,100 and Rs 2,490/sqft. ALSO FLAG THE GEOCODE: 12.834, 79.704 is Kanchipuram town centre — this looks like a registry fallback centroid, not the actual village, so even the location of the 4 plotted layouts we track (Govindharaj Nagar, Pachaiamman Nagar, Sri Ramachandra Nagar, Vijay Nagar — all single-promoter, no RERA number captured) is unconfirmed. Resolve the location before attempting a band.
localities.price_band_note: No apartment market. All 4 tracked records are small single-promoter plotted layouts; no apartment stock found on any portal.
localities.trend_note: No trend series found for Kolivakkam on any reachable source.

localities.name: Thiruverkadu
localities.plot_band_note: Only 2 Thiruverkadu-proper price/area pairs exist (Q1 4,413, Q3 6,606) — both portals' 'Thiruverkadu' plot pages are padded with Vanagaram/Ayappakkam/Poonamallee stock, which I kept out of the band. Band set to 4,600-6,700, bracketing both verified points and consistent with 99acres' land range of Rs 4,900-8,100/sqft and the nobroker forum's Rs 4,150-6,900/sqft. ADJACENT-BELT CONTEXT (excluded from the band): Ayappakkam 3,889-6,498/sqft, Vanagaram 6,994-7,976/sqft, Poonamallee 3,800-4,240/sqft — Thiruverkadu sits between Ayappakkam and Vanagaram, which supports the band's centre. Note Royal Merlion Estate (Vanagaram) is quoted at 8,000/sqft but recomputes to 7,699 on its min and 7,976 on its max — another reminder not to copy quoted rates.
localities.price_band_note: Two recomputed Thiruverkadu-proper projects: Mass Lily (Massbro Developers, Karpagambal Nagar) 2BHK 930 sqft at Rs 54.87L and 3BHK 1,300 sqft at Rs 76.7L, both = Rs 5,900/sqft; SS Square Swasthika (SS Square Property Developers, Mahalakshmi Nagar) 2BHK 918 sqft at Rs 50.49L and 975 sqft at Rs 53.62L, both = Rs 5,500/sqft. Consistent with 99acres' locality flat average of Rs 6,200 and range Rs 4,850-6,750. IMPORTANT: in Thiruverkadu land (4,600-6,700) and built-up (5,300-6,400) are nearly the SAME number. That is normal for the outer west, where low-rise construction cost is low relative to land — but it is exactly the condition that lets the two bands get silently conflated, which is what happened in the existing record.
localities.trend_note: 99acres shows land +13.5% in 1yr, +26.7% in 3yr, +65.2% in 5yr — sustained, driven by the affordable gap between Poonamallee, Avadi and Maduravoyal.
localities.band_audit: MISLABELLED. The existing band 4,850-6,750 is 99acres' APARTMENT (flat) price range for Thiruverkadu, reproduced verbatim — it is a BUILT-UP rate, not land, even though the note bundles 'land Rs 4,900-8,100/sqft' into the same sentence, and the record has 0 apartment projects but 3 plotted layouts tracked. So the band currently measures the wrong product for what this locality actually supplies. My apartment band (5,300-6,400) corroborates that the existing figure is a flat rate. The land band is a genuinely separate number (4,600-6,700) that happens to overlap heavily — which is almost certainly why the conflation went unnoticed.

localities.name: Alandur
localities.plot_band_note: NO PLOT BAND — correctly so. Alandur is a fully built-out inner-suburban locality; we track 0 plotted projects here and 2 apartment projects. No Alandur land price/area pair was found on any reachable source; the only land that changes hands is redevelopment sites transacting off-market. Do NOT copy the apartment band across as a land rate.
localities.price_band_note: Spans a genuinely two-tier market. RECOMPUTED resale/older stock: 3BHK 1,200 sqft at Rs 90L near St Thomas Mount station = Rs 7,500/sqft (chennaiproperties); 2BHK 736 sqft at Rs 70L = 9,511; 2BHK 1,047 sqft at Rs 90L = 8,596; 3BHK 1,083 sqft at Rs 95L = 8,772 (IQR of those four = 7,774-9,326). REPORTED new/under-construction: 99acres flat range Rs 9,850-13,300/sqft with average TRANSACTED rate Rs 10,302/sqft. Band 8,800-12,500 straddles both. DROPPED as a different market: the Guindy/Ekkaduthangal stock that both portals mix into 'Alandur' pages — Appaswamy Malkoha Rs 5.65Cr/2,609 sqft = 21,656/sqft, Sreshta Maudgalya Rs 2.79Cr/1,551 = 17,988, Appaswamy Parkhouse Mews Rs 3.27Cr/1,886 = 17,338, Purva Somerset House Rs 2.95Cr/1,904 = 15,494, Sidharth Solitaire 14,789, SA Simha 14,046. Those are Five Furlong Road / Defence Colony product and are 40-100% above Alandur proper. Also treat nobroker's 'Rs 10,000-20,000/sqft' for Alandur as contaminated by exactly that Guindy stock.
localities.trend_note: ~10-13% appreciation over recent years and +13.93% over 3 years for 2BHK, held up by Alandur Metro (Blue/Green interchange), airport proximity and the Guindy employment spillover.

localities.name: Choolaimedu
localities.plot_band_note: REPORTED ONLY, NOT RECOMPUTED — flagging this honestly. 99acres gives Choolaimedu land at Rs 11,000-17,500/sqft (+6.1% 1yr, +22.4% 3yr) and individual listings quoting Rs 14,115-19,120/sqft, but no reachable source published a total-price/area pair I could recompute, so this band inherits a quoted per-sqft field — the one thing the brief warns against. Treat it as weaker than the apartment band. Directionally it is credible: central-Chennai land trading at ~1.3-1.4x the built-up rate is the normal pattern for a locality being redeveloped plot-by-plot, and we track exactly 1 plotted record here (Lake View Avenue). NOTE the inversion versus the outer belt: in Choolaimedu LAND is worth MORE per sqft than built-up, the opposite of Nemilicheri or Nemmeli.
localities.price_band_note: IQR of 4 recomputed under-construction projects = 11,756-14,125, median 12,500. Rams Apollo (RAMS Real Estates) 2BHK 645 sqft at Rs 77.4L, 656 at Rs 78.72L, 3BHK 976 at Rs 1.17Cr — all Rs 12,000/sqft; Linga Vinayaka (Linga Builders) 3BHK 1,070 at Rs 1.25Cr and 1,200 at Rs 1.4Cr = 11,682/11,667; Karuna (Sreerosh Properties) 2BHK 910 at Rs 1.18Cr and 3BHK 1,400 at Rs 1.82Cr = 12,967/13,000; Hansa Dwaraka (Hansa Estates) 2BHK 1,088 at Rs 1.58Cr and 3BHK 1,277 at Rs 1.85Cr = 14,522/14,487. RESALE IS A DIFFERENT NUMBER: 99acres puts Choolaimedu resale flats at Rs 6,700-11,400/sqft, average Rs 8,150 — while quoting an average TRANSACTED rate of Rs 13,391/sqft, which matches my new-launch field rather than its own resale range. So the honest read is: old walk-up stock Rs 8,000-11,000, new boutique construction Rs 11,700-14,100. DROPPED as a different market: the Aminjikarai/Arumbakkam stock the portal mixes in, notably Taj Skyview Residences at Rs 7.95Cr/2,507 sqft = 31,711/sqft.
localities.trend_note: +5.3% in 1yr and +32.4% over 5yr on flats, land +6.1%/+22.4%; new boutique construction is now asking ~25% above the locality's blended average as old plots redevelop.
localities.band_audit: RIGHT KIND, WRONG LEVEL. The existing band 8,500-12,500 IS an apartment built-up band — not land contamination — and its note correctly cites 99acres/Commonfloor flat rates. But those locality averages are resale-weighted, and the band now understates the market that our tracked projects actually sit in: every under-construction project I recomputed asks 11,675-14,522/sqft, so the existing ceiling of 12,500 is roughly where new stock STARTS. Separately, the existing note has no land figure at all, which is a real gap for a locality where land (Rs 11,000-17,500/sqft) is worth more per sqft than built-up and where redevelopment economics are the whole story.

localities.name: Nemmeli

localities.name: Mugaiyur
localities.corridor: Far South ECR / Cheyyur belt (dataset says GST Road — this is wrong, see note)
localities.plot_band_note: VERY THIN — TWO DATA POINTS. Do not use this to price a deal; use it only to confirm Mugaiyur is a sub-Rs 1,500/sqft far-belt market. (1) RECOMPUTED: 12,000 sqft parcel at Rs 72L = Rs 600/sqft (sulekha listing) — a large-parcel bulk rate, so a floor rather than a layout-plot rate. (2) QUOTED, not recomputable: Rs 1,250/sqft for DTCP-approved 'Mugaiyur, ECR' plots. Context: Cheyyur budget plots quote Rs 499/sqft for 800 sqft. The >2x spread between my two points is why the band is wide and flagged estimated. Confirm whether this record belongs in a CMA tracker at all before publishing any band for it.

I could not corroborate that an apartment market exists here at all; the record needs verification before any apartment band is attached to this locality.
localities.trend_note: No trend series found for Mugaiyur on any reachable source.

localities.name: Walajabad
localities.plot_band_note: IQR of 15 recomputed comparables (every rate = total price / area, computed by me; no quoted per-sqft field trusted). Market is sharply BIFURCATED, which is why the band is wide: a cheap tier at Rs 450-1,000/sqft (loose plots off the main road, several without gated-layout infrastructure) and a DTCP-approved gated-layout tier clustering tightly at Rs 1,200-1,750/sqft. DROPPED as outliers: (a) a 50-acre parcel listed at Rs 112.5 Cr on Sulekha = Rs 5,165/sqft, implausible for Walajabad raw land and almost certainly a mis-keyed listing or a non-residential parcel; (b) Royale Residency at Rs 2,499/sqft is retained in comparables but sits above the IQR as the top-of-market premium layout. NOTE: Sulekha's own per-sqft field was again unreliable here, confirming the known trap.

Its flaw is range, not type: it captures only the DTCP-approved gated-layout tier and omits the substantial sub-Rs 1,000/sqft loose-plot tier that makes up roughly a third of live listings. Recommend widening the floor to ~650.
localities.trend_note: Retains the cooling call from the existing record: the June 2026 cancellation of the Parandur airport removed the speculative catalyst that drove layout launches here. Genuine Oragadam/Sriperumbudur worker demand persists but resale liquidity on speculative-era plots is the risk.

localities.name: Kelambakkam
localities.plot_band_note: IQR of 23 named layouts, each rate recomputed by me as total price / area. Best-evidenced locality in this batch. DROPPED as outliers: VGK Ashbourne Park (Rs 6,998/sqft) and Adityaram Empire (Rs 6,070/sqft) — both premium gated villa-plot product priced off the ECR/coastal comparison set, not the OMR plotted-land market; and Villa Green Vista (Rs 1,670/sqft) at the bottom, a far-fringe farm-plot-style product. Confirmed roofandfloor's flat-rate behaviour: min_price/min_size == max_price/max_size on every layout, so the price range carries no extra information. IMPORTANT: housing.com advertises 'Kelambakkam plots Rs 7.0k/sqft' — that figure is just the single VGK Ashbourne Park listing (its 807-1310 sqft range matches exactly), not an average. No contamination. The existing note's parenthetical plot guess (~Rs 2,500-4,500) also holds up well against my measured plot IQR of 2,750-4,150. This is the cleanest pre-existing record of the eight.
localities.trend_note: South-OMR absorption node; heavy branded-developer entry (Casagrand, Provident, Purva all live simultaneously) is pulling the launch tier up while older stock lags, which is what widens the apartment band.

localities.name: Gerugambakkam
localities.plot_band_note: IQR of 9 comparables, rates recomputed by me. Unusually TIGHT band — this is a land-constrained infill suburb next to Porur/Manapakkam, so plotted supply is scarce and priced consistently. DROPPED: VTB Kuberan Garden (Madras City Properties) — its listing fails the flat-rate test that every other roofandfloor layout passes (min endpoint recomputes to Rs 9,069/sqft, max endpoint to Rs 7,357/sqft, quoted field says Rs 7,200), so the size or price range is mis-keyed and no reliable rate can be extracted. Also excluded from the IQR: an individual 1,200 sqft plot at Rs 96L (Rs 8,000/sqft), the top-end outlier. NOTE: land here is ~85-90% of built-up rate, far above the usual Chennai ratio where land is roughly a third of built-up — a genuine feature of this pocket, not a data error.

Range spans budget compact stock (Karal Babylon Rs 6,000, ARA Vinesh Enclave Rs 5,800) up to Navins Sadhprabha Rs 8,586 and DAC Millennium Rs 8,436. housing.com quotes 'Rs 8.49k/sqft' for Gerugambakkam flats — that tracks the top of the market only, not a central estimate.
localities.band_audit: The existing band [5950, 9200] is CONTAMINATED — it is a mix of two different measurements, not an apartment band. Its floor of 5,950 is literally a LAND asking rate: it matches, to the rupee, a single 1,000 sqft plot listed at Rs 59.5L on roofandfloor. Its ceiling of 9,200 is a top-end apartment asking rate. So the band splices a land rate to a flat rate and labels the result an apartment band. The existing note is self-contradictory in the same way — it states an avg flat rate of ~8,200 and land of 6,450-7,800, neither of which produces the band [5950, 9200]. Recommend replacing with the two separated bands above: land 5,900-6,400, built-up 6,600-7,850.
localities.trend_note: Fastest-appreciating pocket in the Porur-Kundrathur corridor on the strength of DLF Cybercity/L&T employment adjacency; scarce plotted supply keeps land rates abnormally close to built-up rates.

localities.name: Urapakkam
localities.plot_band_note: IQR of 10 named layouts, rates recomputed by me. Distribution is BIMODAL and the IQR deliberately straddles the gap: a fringe cluster at Rs 2,150-2,850 (Mangals Green Paradise, KPN Marvel Township, KPN Sundharam Garden — smaller plots, set back from GST Road toward the Guduvancheri/Maraimalai Nagar side) and a main GST-corridor cluster at Rs 4,500-5,400 (KPN Sri Bhavani Amman Nagar, Premier Kurinji Nagar, Taasa Signature, Sri Bhagya NCR). There is almost nothing trading between 2,900 and 4,400, so treat the band as covering two sub-markets rather than one continuum — distance to GST Road is the variable that decides which one a plot sits in.
localities.price_band_note: Apartment BUILT-UP rate. IQR of 10 live projects, rates recomputed by me. COVERAGE FLAG for the parent: our dataset tracks ZERO apartment projects in Urapakkam, but roofandfloor carries 10 live ones (Frontier Constructions, KPN, Ruby Builders, Sarvajith, MMA, Alameen and others). Urapakkam has a real, established mid-budget apartment market and our RERA registry coverage is materially under-representing it — worth a targeted registry sweep.
localities.band_audit: The existing band [5000, 6500] is correctly TYPED as an apartment built-up band — no land contamination, and the existing note is right that plotted layouts trade lower. But it is set roughly 20-25% too HIGH. Against 10 live projects, only two clear Rs 6,000/sqft (Sri Park View at 6,999 and Ruby Orchid at 6,118); the working market sits at 4,100-5,500 and the measured IQR is 4,300-5,375. The existing note's plot estimate of '~3000-4500' is close to my measured 3,250-4,750 and holds up well.
localities.trend_note: Kilambakkam bus terminus and GST Road/suburban rail keep end-user demand steady, but a large launch pipeline between Urapakkam and Guduvancheri caps how fast rates can move — appreciation is real but end-user-led, not investor-led.

localities.name: West Chennai
localities.plot_band_note: NOT A LOCALITY — this is a directional zone label, not a micro-market, and no price band should ever be attached to it. It spans everything from Porur and Iyyappanthangal to Poonamallee, Sriperumbudur and Kundrathur, whose land rates differ by more than 4x. Any single band here would be meaningless.
localities.price_band_note: Same reason — a zone-level apartment band would be misleading. Because they are curated they are supposed to carry pricing and drive the persona lenses, so leaving them parked under an unpriceable zone label costs us real lens coverage. localities.band_audit: No pre-existing band to audit (existing_price_band was null), and correctly so — this entry should not have a price band at all. Recommend retiring 'West Chennai' as a locality and re-homing its two projects.
